context: Daichi has minor back pain; Saito advises rest and stretching.
purpose: Doctor giving practical medical advice to friend.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Doctor, my back's been killing me.
lines.style: Kansai warmth with an undertone of resignation. Gentle opening, slightly raspy on the complaint itself. Slow, deliberate pacing — not rushing the discomfort. A small sigh buried in the delivery.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.style: Clear, professional inquiry without coldness. Slight lean-forward in the voice — she's listening, not just checking boxes. Measured pace, genuine attention underneath the clinical question.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Three days ago, and it hasn't let up.
lines.style: Kansai directness without complaint. Matter-of-fact tone — stating facts, not seeking sympathy. Steady pacing, slight heaviness on 'hasn't let up' as acknowledgment of duration.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: 休んで、軽く伸ばしてください。
lines.en: Rest it and do some gentle stretching.
lines.style: Calm, assured without being authoritative. Slight emphasis on 'gentle' — protective phrasing, not commanding. Warm professional tone, the voice of someone who knows her patients need reassurance as much as instruction.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 無理せん方がええんですね。
lines.en: So I shouldn't push it, then.
lines.style: Kansai man checking his understanding, quietly relieved. Slight uptilt at the end — affirmation-seeking but not anxious. Warm, genuine tone of someone accepting practical wisdom.

lines.speaker: saito_doctor
lines.jp: はい、一週間、様子見ましょう。
lines.en: Right. Let's monitor it over the next week.
lines.style: Gentle confidence. Steady, measured pacing — conveying stability and a clear path forward. Warmth underneath the professionalism. The reassurance of a plan.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.style: Kansai gratitude, genuine and unhurried. Warm closing, appreciative without effusiveness. Slight settling-back in the tone — relief and trust combined. Genuine small smile in the voice.
